title: The Cure That Killed George Washington
style: Stylized realistic 3D CGI animation still, high-end animated explainer look, Pixar-meets-realism, cinematic soft lighting, detailed skin, hair and fabric, expressive faces, shallow depth of field, no text, no letters, no gore, vertical 9:16 framing.

sections.name: The Cure That Killed George Washington

lines.prompt: An elderly George Washington-like gentleman with white hair lying sick in a canopy bed in 1799, candlelight, worried doctors in dark coats around him

lines: In 1799, the first president of the United States woke up with a terrible sore throat.

lines.prompt: An 18th-century doctor holding a small lancet over a patient's bare forearm while an assistant holds a brass bowl beneath, candlelit bedroom

lines: His doctors did what doctors had done for two thousand years. They cut him, and let him bleed.

lines.prompt: An ancient Greek physician in a toga pointing at a scroll showing four coloured circles, marble columns behind

lines: The idea came from ancient Greece. Illness was blamed on too much of one of your body's four fluids.

lines.prompt: Several brass bowls lined up on a wooden table beside a sickbed in candlelight, doctors whispering in the background

lines: Over about twelve hours, they drained around forty percent of his blood.

lines.prompt: The elderly gentleman lying pale and very weak in the canopy bed, a single candle burning low, a clock on the wall

lines: That night, he died. Many historians think the bleeding made him weaker, and helped kill him.

lines.prompt: A modern nurse in scrubs smiling and holding up a blood donation bag in a bright clinic

lines: Today, doctors only remove blood for a handful of rare conditions. And they take a lot less.
